Any resources you suggest on modular building?

Depends on the application, but it it's simple things, like DIY furniture, one of the best free resources is one of the books that has been a big inspiration for me; Ken Isaacs' How To Build Your Own Living Structures. This book describes the simple 2x2 stick building system called Matrix that later evolced into Box Beam that was popular with eco-tech experimenters in the '70s and was revived more recently as Grid Beam. Box Beam was eventually superceded among experimenters by the advent of extruded alloy T-slot profiles like 80:20, Bosch, and MK profile. But those remain expensive and so use of Matrix continues to be very practical for low-cost building. Isaacs devised Matrix as the DIY building basis of what he called Living Structures and what I like to refer to today as 'furnitecture'; furniture that bridges the line to architecture through adaptive volumetric structures. He was also keen on the use of pipe fitting systems like Kee Klamp and performed many early experiments in microhousing. The book is significant in design and Maker history as it helped inspire the Urban Nomad movement that resulted in all that nomadic 'hippy' furniture design based on repurposing industrial cost-offs like cable spools, oil drums and so on--ultimately leading to today's trend in adaptive reuse and cargotecture; the conversion of shipping containers.

Another useful resource is the N55 web site This design group in Denmark is well known in the Maker world and their simple space frame systems offer a lot of possibilities. They don't document their designs consistently and some of their work relies on advanced crafting resources that aren't typically available in the US--like on-demand custom rotomolding. But they usually provide enough photographs of their work to make reverse-engineering what they're doing relatively easy, making their online manuals a useful resource.

There's also the Global Village Construction Set of the Open Source Ecology project. This is a bit less focused on modular building and more on the development of a modular systems package for subsistence living.

There are many possible modular building systems for people to freely use, but they're not well documented, hence my interest in doing a book cataloging them. There are various box and space frame systems, geodesic dome systems, joining systems intended for use with laser cut and CNC routed fabrication, plate chassis systems deriving from classic clockwork and electronics, Meccano/Erector like systems, modular box/block systems, and even a furniture-scale form of Lego. It's an interesting subject.
